objective: Produce the next sprint plan for Applywright against the current tree, bounded to work that can be executed by DSH implementation agents and reviewed by Codex.

tasks.brief: Read the supplied project documents and the current tree, then produce a bounded next-sprint plan. The product is a CV scoring and grounded-tailoring web app; the repository is its own git repo inside projects/applywright and is not a hub package. Determine what is genuinely unfinished from docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md, cross-check every claim against the code (do not trust prose that says something shipped), and return: (a) the five highest-value items with file paths, (b) for each, the acceptance check a stranger could run, (c) which items are blocked on Johan (DNS, Stripe keys, VAT, Scale-tier decision), (d) an execution order with dependencies. Do not implement, do not edit files and do not delegate further.
acceptance: Five prioritised items, each naming concrete file paths.
Every item has an acceptance check that is a command or an observable behaviour.
Blocked-on-operator items are separated from actionable ones.
Claims about what has shipped cite a file or commit that supports them.
